strengths: Well-motivated biological insight that perturbation responses are coordinated at the program level rather than gene-wise; effectively demonstrated in Figure 1
Comprehensive experimental validation across two benchmarks with rigorous comparison against 13 strong baselines and multiple evaluation metrics (ρ∆, ρ∆D, ACC∆, ACC∆D, DES, PDS, L2, MSE, MAE)
Particularly strong results on out-of-distribution generalization tasks (e.g., 38.0% improvement over CellFlow on ρ∆D for unseen single perturbations in holdout setting)
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 4a-4e) systematically validate each component and demonstrate their synergistic contributions
Biological validation through pathway enrichment analysis (Figures 8-9) and mechanistic case studies (Figure 4) confirm discovered modules align with known biological pathways
Excellent reproducibility: detailed algorithms (1-3), comprehensive implementation details in appendix (A.3), low standard deviations across seeds (Tables 7-8), and code in supplementary materials
Clean, modular framework design with clear three-stage architecture; well-presented with informative figures and logical flow
Robustness analysis demonstrating stable results across multiple random seeds and datasets
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: GRC uses standard balanced assignment via optimal transport; GCAE is incremental Perceiver-style bottleneck; conditional flow matching borrowed from concurrent work (Klein et al. 2025); biological losses are established techniques. Contribution is primarily in combination rather than fundamental innovation

Static module induction may miss context-specific regulatory rewiring: GRC partitions genes offline independent of perturbation condition or cell state; no analysis of module stability across different perturbations; authors acknowledge this limitation (§A.6) but it's a significant biological assumption

Heavy dependence on external priors (GeneCompass embeddings, STRING PPI at threshold 700, Reactome pathways) with limited robustness analysis; performance would degrade with poor embeddings or incomplete databases; Table 4e shows embedding sensitivity
Balanced cluster size constraint (uniform |c_k| = G/K) enforces artificial homogeneity potentially misaligned with true biological program distributions; no validation this reflects reality

Evaluation limited to two mammalian cell line datasets (K562, RPE1) with CRISPR perturbations; no cross-dataset generalization, evaluation on other perturbation modalities, or assessment on diverse cell types; limits generalizability claims

Modest improvements on several key metrics: 7.7% over CellFlow on ρ∆ (Table 1) and 5.9% on DES; improvements on RPE1 less compelling as baselines are weaker overall; unclear if gains justify method complexity

GRC optimization lacks convergence analysis: alternating Sinkhorn + rounding solved offline without analysis of convergence properties, local minima, or initialization sensitivity; number of iterations T unspecified
Incomplete technical details: tie-breaking in arg max assignment, Stage 1 convergence criterion, pathway activation computation in Eq. 8, handling of genes absent from PPI/pathway databases
Method complexity with five key components and numerous hyperparameters (λ_corr, λ_pathway, K, M, etc.) may hinder adoption; limited guidance on hyperparameter setting for new datasets
Interpretability analysis limited to qualitative case studies (Fig. 4) on two perturbations; no systematic analysis of which modules drive predictions or statistical validation of attention patterns

strengths: Well-motivated biological insight addressing genuine limitation of gene-wise modeling in prior work
Technically solid framework integrating GRC, GCAE, and structure-aware objectives in principled manner
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (Norman, RPE1, ComboSciPlex), metrics, and evaluation settings (additive/holdout splits)
Strong and consistent empirical results with 6.7% average improvement, particularly pronounced on OOD generalization (38% on unseen single genes)
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 6a-6e) isolating contributions of individual components and design choices
Robust statistical validation including paired Wilcoxon tests and analysis across random seeds with low variance
Clear presentation with effective figures and extensive supplementary material including full algorithms, hyperparameters, and implementation details
Honest discussion of limitations (A.8) and acknowledgment of dependencies on external priors
Functional enrichment analysis (Figure 3) validates that induced clusters are biologically coherent
Promising results on cross-cell-line transfer and drug perturbations suggesting generalization beyond single dataset
weaknesses: Static module structure cannot adapt to perturbation context; biological programs likely reorganize under different conditions but scBIG partitions remain fixed
Balanced cluster size constraint (|c_k|=G/K) justified as 'architectural regularizer' but may not reflect biological reality where modules should have varying sizes

Heavy dependence on external resources (GeneCompass embeddings, STRING PPI at threshold 700, Reactome pathways) creates brittleness and limits generalization to new organisms/domains where priors incomplete

Limited biological validation: enrichment analysis is post-hoc, perturbation-specific coordination (Table 5) shown only for 3 examples, attention analysis (Figure 4) qualitative with 2 anecdotal cases, no wet-lab validation
Evaluation scope primarily focused on two human cell types (K562 dominant, RPE1); cross-cell-line transfer (Table 18) shows modest improvements suggesting cell-type specificity of modules
Mini-batch OT for pairing control/perturbed cells lacks justification; sensitivity to this choice not analyzed
Linear interpolation path assumption (zt=(1-t)z0+tz1) in flow matching may miss complex dynamics; no analysis of when linearity breaks down
Reconstruction loss (Eq. 5) abandoned after pretraining stage; joint optimization during fine-tuning not explored
Incremental architectural contributions: GCAE is standard Perceiver with dual-stream fusion, structure-aware losses are straightforward, flow matching backbone directly borrowed from CellFlow
Performance bounded by quality of pretrained embeddings and pathway databases; limited ablation on these choices (only Figure 5 for embeddings, no sensitivity to PPI threshold)
Inconsistency between claims to move 'beyond static priors' while fundamentally relying on them
Complex pipeline with multiple components (GRC, GCAE, flow matching, two alignment objectives, two-stage training) may hinder adoption and reproducibility
Hyperparameter selections appear somewhat arbitrary (K=32 chosen empirically, λ_corr=λ_pathway=0.1 set equally despite Table 6d showing sensitivity)
Limited analysis of why scBIG wins—unclear which components contribute most to improvements
